Generated by Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct In longitudinal clinical practice, every chest X-ray is read in the context of the patients prior exam, and much of what the radiologist communicates is the change from one visit to the next. To the best of our knowledge, we present the first training-free best-of-N sampling scheme for pre-trained chest X-ray report generators that is explicitly aware of this longitudinal prior to current transition. We call it transition-aware best-of-N sampling, each report is split into sentences and embedded into an unordered set in Rd; each (prior, current) pair is reduced to a fixed-dim directional vector via a set-to-set distance designed to encode the change between the two sets; and candidates are scored by cosine distance from their candidate transition vector to a cached bank of ground-truth training transition vectors, aggregated as min or kNN. We instantiate the framework with four directional set distances (mean-shift, novelty residual, directed-Hausdorff anchor, and cost-weighted optimal transport) and evaluate on a multi-visit AP-PA cohort, running inference under three prompts on three vision-language generators. Transition-aware best-of-N outperforms random selection across the board, with the largest relative gains on the Impression section.
affiliations: Department of Biomedical Data Science, Stanford University School of Medicine, Stanford, CA, USA
Department of Electrical Engineering, Stanford University, Stanford, CA, USA
Department of Mathematical Modelling, Statistics & Bioinformatics, Ghent University, Ghent, Belgium

ru.title: Генерация отчетов по рентгенограммам с осознанием изменений
ru.desc: В статье представлен новый метод генерации отчетов по рентгенограммам грудной клетки, который не требует обучения. Он использует исторические данные пациентов, акцентируя внимание на изменениях между предыдущими и текущими обследованиями. Метод называется 'переходное осознанное выборка лучшего из N' и эффективно применяет метрики расстояния между наборами. Результаты показывают, что предложенный метод превосходит случайный выбор, особенно в разделе 'Впечатление'.

en.title: Revolutionizing Chest X-Ray Reports with Transition-Aware Sampling
en.desc: This paper introduces a new method for generating chest X-ray reports without the need for additional training. It focuses on the changes in a patient's condition by comparing previous and current X-ray examinations. The method uses a unique sampling technique called transition-aware best-of-N sampling, which evaluates reports based on how well they reflect these changes. The approach outperforms random selection, particularly in the Impression section of the reports, by utilizing set-to-set distance metrics to encode the differences between prior and current examinations.

papers.title: Deform360: A Massive Multi-view Visuotactile Dataset for Deformable World Models
papers.abstract: Abstract A large-scale visuotactile dataset called Deform360 is introduced to study deformable object dynamics, enabling comparison between 2D video and 3D particle world models for robotic manipulation tasks.  Generated by Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct Predicting object dynamics (i.e., world modeling) is a fundamental challenge for robotic manipulation, and modeling deformable objects presents a particularly difficult case due to their high-dimensional state spaces and complex material properties. While current world models approach this through two distinct paradigms: learning the dynamics over the 2D pixel space or more explicit 3D geometric space. A systematic understanding of their relative strengths and limitations remains elusive due to the lack of diverse, large-scale real-world data. To address this, we present Deform360, a large-scale visuotactile dataset featuring 198 daily-life objects, 1,980 interaction sequences, and over 215 hours of observations from 41 surround-view cameras and bimanual tactile grippers to capture both global motion and contact-induced local deformations. Leveraging a novel markerless visuotactile 3D tracking pipeline to extract dense geometry and motion, we systematically evaluate current state-of-the-art world models, comparing 2D video models against 3D particle models. Finally, we provide a preliminary demonstration indicating the real-world applicability of our dataset by performing robot planning tasks on deformable objects. Our analysis reveals key insights into the trade-offs between structural priors and scalability, providing a solid benchmark for future research in generalizable deformable object-centric world modeling. Project website: https://deform360.lhy.xyz
affiliations: Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, MA

ru.title: Исследуем динамику деформируемых объектов!
ru.desc: В статье представлено крупномасштабное датасет Deform360, предназначенное для изучения динамики деформируемых объектов. Этот датасет включает в себя 198 объектов повседневного обихода и более 200 часов наблюдений с использованием камер и тактильных захватов. Авторы сравнивают подходы моделирования динамики объектов в 2D и 3D пространствах и анализируют их сильные и слабые стороны. Результаты показывают важность этого датасета для будущих исследований в области моделирования деформируемых объектов и роботов.

en.title: Unlocking Deformable Object Dynamics with Deform360
en.desc: The paper introduces Deform360, a large-scale visuotactile dataset designed to enhance the understanding of deformable object dynamics for robotic manipulation. It compares two approaches to world modeling: 2D video-based models and 3D particle-based models, highlighting the challenges posed by the complex nature of deformable objects. The dataset includes extensive observations of various daily-life objects, captured through advanced tracking techniques to analyze both global and local deformations. This work aims to provide a benchmark for future research, revealing insights into the trade-offs between different modeling strategies.

papers.title: Bridging Interleaved Multi-Modal Reasoning as a Unified Decision Process
papers.abstract: Abstract BRAID framework enables unified multi-modal reasoning by casting text-image interaction as a Markov decision process, allowing joint optimization through reinforcement learning with vision-language model guidance.  Generated by Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct Unified multi-modal models (UMMs) have shown promising interleaved text-image reasoning capabilities, yet effectively optimizing such multi-turn generation via reinforcement learning (RL) remains an open challenge. Existing approaches apply RL exclusively to text steps, relegating image generation to supervised surrogates, preventing policy gradients from propagating through the full interleaved trajectory across heterogeneous modalities. This leaves the potential of RL for UMMs largely untapped. In the paper, we introduce BRAID (Bridging inteRleAved multI-modal reasoning as a unified Decision process), a simple framework that casts multi-turn text-image-text reasoning as a unified Markov decision process (MDP), enabling joint optimization of textual and visual generation via a single, principled RL objective. BRAID computes a shared trajectory-level advantage and propagates it coherently into both text tokens and image denoising paths, each optimized through its modality-native policy gradient mechanism. To further address long-horizon credit assignment, BRAID employs a vision-language model (VLM) judge that scores each intermediate image on its reasoning utility, supplying dense turn-level feedback to sharpen learning at critical visual branches. Experiments on spatial reasoning and visual perception benchmarks show that BRAID consistently outperforms various baselines, confirming that a unified MDP formulation with vision-thinking guidance is essential for effective multi-modal reasoning.
affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong

ru.title: Объединение многомодального вывода с помощью процесса Маркова
ru.desc: Работа представляет новый подход под названием BRAID, который объединяет текстово-изображенческое взаимодействие в рамках процесса Маркова. Этот метод позволяет совместную оптимизацию текстового и визуального генерации с использованием обучения с подкреплением. BRAID вычисляет общее преимущество на уровне траектории и распространяет его на текстовые токены и пути денойзинга изображений. Эксперименты показывают, что BRAID превосходит существующие методы, подтверждая важность единой формулировки MDP для эффективного многомодального вывода.

en.title: BRAID: Unifying Text-Image Reasoning with Reinforcement Learning
en.desc: The BRAID framework introduces a new way to handle multi-modal reasoning by treating the interaction between text and images as a Markov decision process (MDP). This allows for joint optimization of both text and image generation using reinforcement learning (RL), overcoming limitations of previous methods that only applied RL to text. By computing a shared advantage across the entire reasoning process, BRAID effectively propagates learning signals through both modalities. Experiments demonstrate that this unified approach significantly improves performance in tasks requiring spatial reasoning and visual perception.

papers.title: CONFLUX: A Latent Diusion Model for 3D Chest-CT Synthesis with RL Post-Training
papers.abstract: Abstract A 3D latent diffusion model for chest CT generation that achieves high-fidelity results while enabling control over clinical attributes through metadata conditioning and reinforcement learning refinement.  Generated by Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct Controllable generative models of 3D medical images can synthesize volumes with specified clinical attributes, but this demands samples that are simultaneously high-fidelity, natively 3D, and faithful to the requested conditioning. We present CONFLUX, a latent diffusion model for chest computed tomography (CT): a 3D variational autoencoder compresses each volume, and a rectified-flow transformer generates in the latent space. Generation is conditioned on structured radiological metadata (18 abnormality findings, sex, age, and reconstruction kernel) through adaptive layer normalization. The model leads strong volumetric baselines on tri-planar Frechet distance (FID 32.3 vs. 74.6 for MAISI) while exposing direct control over clinical attributes. To strengthen that control we add an online reinforcement-learning post-training stage (group-relative policy optimization) that rewards how reliably a classifier recovers the requested findings from each generated volume. Judged by a separate, independent classifier, post-training removes 47% of the shortfall relative to real-scan reliability. We release the model and a ~200k synthetic chest-CT dataset with conditioning metadata spanning a wide variety of clinical findings.
affiliations: Department of Biomedical Data Science, Stanford University School of Medicine
Department of Electrical Engineering, Stanford University
Department of Mathematical Modelling, Statistics & Bioinformatics, Ghent University

ru.title: Генерация КТ с управляемыми клиническими характеристиками
ru.desc: В данной статье представлен 3D латентный диффузионный модель для генерации грудных КТ, которая достигает высококачественных результатов и позволяет управлять клиническими характеристиками через условие метаданных. Модель использует вариационный автоэнкодер для сжатия объемов и трансформер для генерации в латентном пространстве. Генерация основывается на структурированных радиологических метаданных, таких как находки аномалий, пол, возраст и параметры реконструкции. Благодаря дополнительному этапу пост-обучения с использованием обучения с подкреплением, модель демонстрирует улучшенные результаты в распознавании клинических находок.

en.title: High-Fidelity 3D Chest CT Generation with Controlled Clinical Attributes
en.desc: This paper presents CONFLUX, a 3D latent diffusion model designed for generating high-fidelity chest CT images. It allows for control over clinical attributes by conditioning on structured metadata, such as abnormality findings and patient demographics. The model utilizes a 3D variational autoencoder for compression and a rectified-flow transformer for generation in the latent space. Additionally, an online reinforcement learning stage enhances the model's ability to produce images that accurately reflect the requested clinical features.

papers.title: Taste-aware music retrieval from audio embeddings
papers.abstract: Abstract Audio encoders from HEAR families are evaluated for taste prediction, with gated late-fusion showing superior rank correlation and the best models achieving human-level accuracy on held-out music.  Generated by Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct Crossmodal correspondences between sound and taste are well established in psychology and neuroscience, but largely absent from content-based multimedia retrieval. We formalise taste-from-audio prediction as a content-based music information retrieval benchmark over a perceptually validated multi-source corpus, comparing ten frozen audio encoders from the four HEAR families under a shared multi-task regression head, with gated late-fusion as a configurable variant. In order to assess the effectiveness of the models, we compute absolute error and rank correlation. The strongest systems predict the five tastes within a macro RMSE of 0.134; on held-out real music their error is less than half a single rater's deviation from the consensus (RMSE 0.13 vs. 0.28), so the model tracks the group consensus more closely than an average human rater, and well below the previous state of the art baseline (0.219). On absolute error the encoders are statistically flat, with a single VGGish matching the best fusion, but gated late-fusion's advantage is confined to rank correlation (macro Pearson r 0.724 vs. 0.666). Operationalised as a content-based retrieval index, the predicted taste space ranks a 309-item pool far more faithfully than a CLAP-text baseline, which sits at chance; ridge probes and an audio-bandstop knockout read the strongest representations against documented sound-taste correspondences.

ru.title: Предсказание вкусов на основе аудио
ru.desc: В данной работе оцениваются аудиокодеры из семейства HEAR для предсказания вкусов. Использование поздней гибридной фузии показало наилучшие результаты в корреляции рангов, а лучшие модели достигают точности на уровне человека на отложенных музыкальных данных. Мы формализуем предсказание вкусов на основе аудио как задачу извлечения информации из музыки и сравниваем десять замороженных аудиокодеров. Результаты показывают, что предложенные модели надежно отражают группу консенсуса лучше, чем среднестатистический оценщик.

en.title: Predicting Taste from Music: A New Benchmark in Audio Analysis
en.desc: This paper explores the use of audio encoders from the HEAR families to predict taste based on music, establishing a new benchmark in content-based music information retrieval. The study employs a multi-task regression approach and evaluates models using metrics like absolute error and rank correlation. Gated late-fusion techniques demonstrate superior performance, achieving human-level accuracy in taste prediction. The findings reveal that the best models closely align with group consensus, outperforming previous benchmarks in this innovative crossmodal task.

papers.title: SynCity 3000: Bootstrapping Scene-Scale 3D Diffusion
papers.abstract: Abstract SynCity 3000 generates large, coherent 3D scenes by adapting image-to-3D generators as convolutional operators through fine-tuning on synthetic scene data.  Generated by Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct We present SynCity 3000, a framework for generating 3D scenes that are globally coherent while enabling fine-grained layout control. Building on the ability of current image-to-3D generators to produce complex 3D assets from a single image, we extend this capability to the scale of entire scenes by adapting the generator to be applicable as a convolutional operator. We achieve this by fine-tuning the model on scene-like data generated by a new synthetic data engine, which we propose to address the scarcity of 3D scene data for training. The convolutional generator is then applied to a dimetric image of the entire scene, generated from the user prompt, resulting in 3D scenes of arbitrary size and complexity. Across diverse prompts and layouts, SynCity 3000 produces large, coherent, and detailed scenes, addressing the shortcomings of prior approaches to 3D scene generation.
affiliations: Visual Geometry Group, University of Oxford

ru.title: Генерация больших согласованных 3D-сцен
ru.desc: SynCity 3000 — это фреймворк для генерации 3D-сцен, который обеспечивает глобальную согласованность и контроль над компоновкой. Он адаптирует генераторы изображений в 3D, используя свёрточные операторы и дообучение на синтетических данных сцен. Это позволяет создавать сложные 3D-активы из одного изображения и масштабировать процесс до целых сцен. Благодаря новым методам генерации синтетических данных, SynCity 3000 преодолевает недостаток 3D-данных для обучения и достигает больших, согласованных и детализированных сцен.

en.title: Revolutionizing 3D Scene Generation with SynCity 3000
en.desc: SynCity 3000 is a framework designed to generate large and coherent 3D scenes by fine-tuning image-to-3D generators. It adapts these generators to work as convolutional operators, allowing for detailed control over scene layouts. The model is trained on synthetic scene data to overcome the lack of available 3D scene datasets. By using a dimetric image from user prompts, SynCity 3000 can create complex 3D environments of various sizes and intricacies.

papers.title: AI Wizards at EXIST 2026: Hierarchical Soft-Label Learning for Multimodal Sexism Identification in Memes
papers.abstract: Abstract A multimodal sexism identification system for memes uses hierarchical conditional soft-label prediction with vision-language embeddings and a lightweight Gated MLP trained via KL divergence and uncertainty weighting.  Generated by Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct We present the AI Wizards submission to EXIST 2026 for multimodal sexism identification in memes. The task is composed of three, increasingly harder subtasks. We model them hierarchically as conditional soft-label prediction over empirical annotator distributions. Our system maps fixed Gemini Embedding 2 vision-language representations through a lightweight Gated MLP trained with KL divergence and homoscedastic uncertainty weighting. Our submissions ranked first on Task 2.3 and fourth on Tasks 2.1 and 2.2 on the official Soft-Soft leaderboards. The code is available at https://github.com/NLP-AI-Wizards/EXIST-2026
affiliations: Everest Systems GmbH, Max-Jarecki-Straße 21, 69115 Heidelberg, Germany
Swiss Data Science Center, ETH Zürich, Andreasturm, Andreasstrasse 5, 8092 Zürich, Switzerland

ru.title: Идентификация сексизма в мемах с помощью ИИ
ru.desc: В данной статье представлен многофункциональный метод идентификации сексизма в мемах. Система использует иерархическое предсказание условных мягких меток с помощью векторных представлений изображения и текста. Обучение происходит с использованием KL-дивергенции и взвешивания неопределенности. Мы достигли лучших результатов в определенных задачах соревнования EXIST 2026.

en.title: Harnessing Multimodal AI for Sexism Detection in Memes
en.desc: This paper presents a system for identifying sexism in memes using multiple types of data, known as multimodal analysis. It employs a hierarchical approach to predict soft labels based on the distributions of human annotators. The system utilizes vision-language embeddings and a lightweight Gated MLP, which is trained using techniques like KL divergence and uncertainty weighting. The authors achieved top rankings in specific tasks of the competition, demonstrating the effectiveness of their model.

papers.title: Speaker-Disentangled Chunk-Wise Regression for Syllabic Tokenization
papers.abstract: Abstract A speaker-disentangled syllabic tokenizer regresses perturbed student representations toward clean teacher targets to improve syllable boundary detection and speech language modeling performance.  Generated by Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct Unsupervised syllabic tokenization aims to learn discrete syllabic tokens that capture latent linguistic content-related structure from raw speech. Recent syllabic tokenization methods employ teacher-student distillation of the pretrained HuBERT to organize latent speech frame representations into syllabic segments. However, when trained with an utterance-level cross-entropy objective, the model predicts speaker identity rather than linguistic content, thereby compromising the purity of syllabic tokens. To address this problem, we propose a speaker-disentangled syllabic tokenizer that regresses speaker-perturbed student representations toward clean teacher targets within fixed-length chunks. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance in syllable boundary detection and syllabic segment clustering. Moreover, a speech language model trained on our syllabic tokens achieves a 7% relative improvement in syntactic and semantic understanding over the phone-level SpiRit-LM.
affiliations: Institute of Science Tokyo, Meguro, Tokyo 152-8550, Japan
National Institute of Information and Communications Technology, Kyoto 619-0289, Japan

ru.title: Выделение слогов без учета говорящего
ru.desc: В данной статье представлен токенизатор, который отделяет слоги от конкретного говорящего, чтобы улучшить обнаружение границ слогов и модели языка речи. Метод основан на дистилляции знаний от учителя к студенту, чтобы организовать представления речи в слоговые сегменты. Проблема в том, что предшествующие методы часто фокусируются на идентификации говорящего, а не на лингвистическом содержании, что ухудшает качество токенов. Новый подход демонстрирует выдающиеся результаты в обнаружении границ слогов и кластеризации слогов.

en.title: Enhancing Syllable Detection with Speaker-Disentangled Tokenization
en.desc: This paper introduces a speaker-disentangled syllabic tokenizer that enhances the detection of syllable boundaries and improves speech language modeling. It uses a teacher-student distillation approach to refine syllabic tokens from raw speech, focusing on linguistic content rather than speaker identity. By regressing perturbed student representations towards clean teacher targets, the model effectively organizes speech frame representations into coherent syllabic segments. Experimental results show that this method outperforms previous techniques, achieving significant improvements in both syllable boundary detection and language understanding tasks.

papers.title: Speaker-Aware Temporal Aggregation Strategies on Segment Representations for Depression Detection in Dyadic Interaction: A Benchmark Study
papers.abstract: Abstract Temporal aggregation methods for speech-based depression detection show inconsistent performance across different backbones and training runs, highlighting the need for robust benchmarking criteria.  Generated by Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct Speech-based depression detection compresses features from short audio segments into one speaker-level decision, a step called temporal aggregation rarely studied on its own. Most benchmarks fix a single self-supervised encoder and a single hand-picked layer, so a reported gain may reflect the pipeline rather than the aggregation method itself. We introduce DEPOOL, a controlled benchmark that compares six aggregation architectures with six frozen speech backbones on an English and a Mandarin depression corpus, where each configuration learns which backbone layers matter rather than fixing one by hand. Across the resulting 72-configuration grid, a third of configurations collapse into predicting a single class for every speaker, a failure tied to the backbone as much as to the method, and the architecture that is most stable in a single-seed run becomes unreliable when training repeats across seeds. Robustness to backbone and seed, rather than average accuracy across a single pipeline, should be a first-class benchmarking criterion for temporal aggregation in clinical speech.
affiliations: Ming Hsieh Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, University of Southern California, USA
Signal Analysis and Interpretation Laboratory (SAIL), University of Southern California, USA

ru.title: Надежные методы агрегации для выявления депрессии по речи
ru.desc: В данной статье рассматриваются методы временной агрегации для обнаружения депрессии на основе речи, которые показывают непостоянную эффективность в зависимости от используемых моделей и условий обучения. Авторы представляют DEPOOL, новый контрольный бенчмарк, который сравнивает различные архитектуры агрегации с несколькими фиксированными речевыми моделями на корповом материале на английском и мандаринском языках. Исследование показывает, что многие конфигурации не могут правильно классифицировать речь, а стабильные архитектуры при одном запуске оказываются ненадежными при повторной тренировке. Это подчеркивает важность учета устойчивости к используемым моделям и условиям обучения при оценке методов временной агрегации в клиническом контексте.

en.title: Enhancing Robustness in Speech-Based Depression Detection
en.desc: This paper addresses the challenges in speech-based depression detection, particularly focusing on the temporal aggregation methods used to combine short audio segments into a single decision. The authors introduce DEPOOL, a benchmarking framework that evaluates various aggregation architectures across different speech backbones and languages. They find that many configurations fail to generalize, often predicting a single class for all speakers, which highlights the influence of both the aggregation method and the backbone used. The study emphasizes the importance of robustness to variations in backbone and training seeds as key criteria for evaluating temporal aggregation methods in clinical applications.

papers.title: Look Before You Leap: Distilling Tree Search into Action Evaluation for Frozen VLA Models
papers.abstract: Abstract A framework called SVA is introduced that enhances Vision-Language-Action models by decoupling action generation from consequence evaluation, thereby improving generalization and task success rates while reducing computational costs.  Generated by Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models acquire broad embodied capabilities through large-scale pretraining, yet their generalization remains far more fragile than that of LLMs and VLMs. The prevailing remedy, post-training via supervised fine-tuning or reinforcement learning, improves task-specific performance but narrows the generalist capability that makes pretraining valuable. We identify a key bottleneck: VLA failures stem not only from action generation but also from action evaluation. A diagnostic pass@k study confirms that frozen VLAs already contain competent behaviors in their output distribution, with overall success rates rising from 33% at pass@1 to 92% at pass@32. Inspired by this, we propose SVA (Search, Value, and Act), a simple framework that equips frozen VLA policies with long-term consequence awareness. SVA first uses Monte-Carlo tree search in simulation to fully explore the VLA's output distribution and collect diverse trajectories annotated with empirical returns; this knowledge is then distilled into a lightweight Q-value model that predicts the expected consequence of candidate actions; at deployment, the frozen VLA proposes multiple candidates and the evaluator selects the one with the highest uncertainty-regularized Q-value, requiring no simulator access. By decoupling action proposal from consequence evaluation, SVA preserves the generalization capacity of the VLA backbone while substantially improving task success rates. Experiments across embodied benchmarks show that SVA consistently improves generalization on unseen tasks and exhibits strong test-time scaling behavior. Strikingly, SVA enables a 9B VLA to outperform a 27B VLA by 7 points at 27% lower inference latency, suggesting that scaling test-time evaluation is more cost-effective than scaling model size.
affiliations: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences

ru.title: SVA: Улучшаем модели через отделение действий и последствий
ru.desc: В статье представлена новая структура SVA, которая улучшает модели Vision-Language-Action, отделяя генерацию действий от оценки последствий. Это позволяет повысить обобщающую способность моделей и успех выполнения задач, а также снизить вычислительные затраты. Применяя метод Монте-Карло для исследования выходного распределения VLA, SVA собирает разнообразные траектории и извлекает знания для создания легковесной модели Q-значений. В результате SVA показывает значительное улучшение результатов на новых задачах, сохраняя при этом общие возможности базовой модели VLA.

en.title: Decoupling Actions for Smarter Decision-Making in VLA Models
en.desc: The paper introduces a framework called SVA that improves Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models by separating action generation from consequence evaluation. This separation enhances the models' ability to generalize across tasks and increases their success rates while lowering computational costs. The SVA framework utilizes Monte-Carlo tree search to explore action outputs and create a Q-value model that predicts the outcomes of actions. By doing this, SVA allows for better decision-making without needing to access a simulator, leading to improved performance even with smaller models.

papers.title: PixCon: Clean-Positive Contrastive Learning for Foundation-Model Semi-Supervised Segmentation
papers.abstract: Abstract PixCon is a semi-supervised semantic segmentation framework that uses clean-positive pixel-contrastive learning with per-class memory banks to improve accuracy over existing methods.  Generated by Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct Semi-supervised semantic segmentation (SSSS) has long turned on one question, which pseudo-labels to trust, and answered it with ever more careful confidence filtering. Foundation backbones change the regime: with a DINOv2 teacher a strict threshold already retains a measured 98%-clean pseudo-label set, so the accuracy that remains lives not in the filter but in how the embedding space is structured by class. We propose PixCon, a clean-positive pixel-contrastive framework. PixCon maintains a per-class memory bank that admits only labeled pixels the student already classifies correctly, guaranteeing a contamination-free positive set (ρ_F=0) by construction, unlike prior contrastive SSSS banks (ReCo, U^2PL) built from confidence-filtered pseudo-labels. It is a single branch over a consistency backbone, adds no inference-time parameters, and needs no bank-specific threshold. A first-order analysis of the supervised-InfoNCE gradient explains why contamination hurts: its false-positive term scales as ρ_F/(1-ρ_F), which we measure (0.018 on Pascal, 0.106 on ADE20K) rather than assume. Across Pascal VOC, Cityscapes, and ADE20K, PixCon matches or improves a strong DINOv2-based UniMatch V2 baseline in a compute-matched one-switch protocol: it improves every Pascal-1/8 seed (a per-seed gain of about +0.2 mIoU) and its three-seed mean reaches 87.90, the published UniMatch V2-B figure. Because contamination is already rare under foundation-model teachers, our analysis indicates the ρ_F=0 guarantee acts chiefly as robustness as teachers weaken, while the accuracy gain comes from cleaner positive supervision, making clean-positive contrast a robust, low-cost default for foundation-model SSSS.

ru.title: Чистая контрастная семантическая сегментация
ru.desc: PixCon - это полусупервизированная структура для семантической сегментации, которая использует чистое положительное пиксельно-контрастное обучение. Она применяет память по классам, чтобы поддерживать только корректно классифицированные пиксели, обеспечивая тем самым отсутствие загрязнения в положительном наборе данных. В результате PixCon достигает или даже превосходит точность существующих методов на известных наборах данных. Это делает его надежным и экономически эффективным решением для задач полусупервизированной семантической сегментации.

en.title: Clean-Positive Contrast for Better Segmentation
en.desc: PixCon is a new framework for semi-supervised semantic segmentation that enhances accuracy by using clean-positive pixel-contrastive learning. It introduces per-class memory banks that only include correctly classified labeled pixels, ensuring a contamination-free positive set. This approach eliminates the need for complex confidence filtering and additional parameters during inference. The results show that PixCon outperforms existing methods, providing a robust and efficient solution for improving segmentation tasks with foundation models.

papers.title: Learning to Trigger: Reinforcement Learning at the Large Hadron Collider
papers.abstract: Abstract Reinforcement learning agents optimize real-time trigger thresholds at particle colliders by adapting Group-Filtered Policy Optimization to streaming control, improving signal efficiency and background rate management on both simulated and real collision data.  Generated by Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct High-throughput scientific facilities such as the Large Hadron Collider depend on real-time event filtering (triggering) under tight constraints on bandwidth, latency, and storage. In practice, trigger menus are largely static and hand-tuned and can become suboptimal as detector conditions, pileup, and background composition drift over time. We cast online threshold tuning as a sequential decision-making problem: a reinforcement learning agent ingests streaming summaries of recent rates and signal-sensitive features and updates trigger thresholds to maximize signal efficiency while tracking a target background rate within a tolerance band. We adapt Group-Filtered Policy Optimization (GFPO) to streaming control and introduce two variants (GFPO-F, GFPO-FR) that enforce background rate feasibility during training. On a benchmark that emulates realistic collider operation, we study two representative triggers: a total transverse energy (H_{T}) trigger sensitive to pileup variation, and an anomaly-detection (AD) trigger based on reconstruction loss for rare or non-standard signatures. On Monte Carlo streams, our agent increases the fraction of in-tolerance time intervals by 48\% (H_T) and 28\% (AD), with a cumulative gain of up to 2\% in signal efficiency on those in-tolerance intervals. Transferring from simulation to real collision data (CMS Run 283408), the same agent, without fine-tuning, achieves a 56\% (H_T) and 28\% (AD) in-tolerance improvement over baselines, with further signal-efficiency gain on both triggers. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of RL-based trigger control on real Large Hadron Collider collision data. Code is available at https://github.com/Zixind/GFPO_LHC (see repo for details).

ru.title: Оптимизация триггеров с помощью обучения с подкреплением
ru.desc: В этой работе рассматривается использование агентного обучения с подкреплением для оптимизации порогов триггеров в коллайдерах частиц в режиме реального времени. Адаптируя метод Group-Filtered Policy Optimization (GFPO), авторы улучшают эффективность сигналов и управление фоновыми rate на симулированных и реальных данных столкновений. Агент обучается обновлять пороги триггеров, основываясь на потоковых данных, чтобы максимизировать эффективность сигналов при контроле фонового уровня. Результаты показывают значительное улучшение в интервалах допустимого фона и сигналов без дополнительной настройки для реальных данных.

en.title: Dynamic Trigger Optimization in Particle Colliders Using Reinforcement Learning
en.desc: This paper presents a method for optimizing real-time trigger thresholds in particle colliders using reinforcement learning. The authors adapt Group-Filtered Policy Optimization to handle streaming control, allowing the agent to dynamically adjust thresholds based on incoming data. By framing the problem as a sequential decision-making task, the agent improves signal efficiency while managing background rates effectively. The results show significant improvements in both simulated and real collision data, marking a novel application of reinforcement learning in high-energy physics.
